# Review — aeneid-041 (Aeneid VI.98–189), adversarial reviewer

Two passes. Pass 1: every unit's `l`, `i`, `n` against the Latin word by word; every grammatical label; speech marks; remembered English. Pass 2: re-read the edited units, then hand-scanned all 92 lines (quantities, not just flagged ones), and checked every new `scan-fixes.json` entry against the build's word-match rule and the validator's foot pattern. `t` untouched (all 51 units still equal the source cut); `units.json` regenerated by `make_units.py`. Speech marks: 3 opening, 3 closing in each of t, l, i (opens at 103, 125, 187; closes at 123, 155 [see refusal R1], 189).

**Severity counts: major 6, medium 14, low 14. Refused findings: 7 (listed at the end).**

## Changes

### Major
1. **6.118 scan wrong** (scanner cost 0.5, unflagged). `lucis` is lūcīs (long ū, dative plural -īs) and `Hecate` is Hĕ-că-tē; scanner had lu- short and He-ca- long. Hand scansion added.
2. **6.147 scan wrong** (cost 0.0). `te` (pronoun) is long, `fata` has long ā, `vocant` has short o; scanner had te, fa short and ta, vo long. Hand scansion added.
3. **6.183 scan wrong** (cost 1.3). Scanner made `opera`'s o long and `Aeneas` Ae-ne-as with short ne/as. Hand scansion: Nec non | Ae-ne | as o-pe | in-ter | ta-li-a | pri-mus.
4. **Note 106–109 (Acheronte refuso)**: "ablative of description" is false; it is an ablative absolute ("Acheron having been poured back"). Fixed.
5. **Note 106–109 (ad conspectum… et ora)**: "both governed by 'genitoris'" is false (both follow `ad`; `genitoris` is the genitive depending on them). Fixed.
6. **Note 127 (patet)**: "The verb is in the singular, as a regular statement of what is always so" is false; it is singular because `ianua` is. Fixed.

### Medium
7–10. **Scan, initial Ae- split by the scanner**: 6.103, 6.156, 6.169, 6.176 (Aeneas/Aeneae as A-e-ne). Hand scansions added (Ae-nē-ās / Ae-nē-ae, as at 1.170, 1.220).
11. **Note 119–122**: "Orpheus has two syllables, with synizesis" mislabels it; it is the Greek diphthong eu. Fixed.
12. **Note 149–151**: `exanimum`/`exanimem` called "the same word in different case forms"; they are the two forms (exanimus/exanimis) of the adjective. Fixed.
13. **Note 162–165**: "two infinitives of respect" after `praestantior`; relabelled epexegetic (explanatory) infinitives.
14. **Note 154–155**: `Stygis` called "a Greek genitive"; it is the ordinary genitive of Styx. Fixed.
15. **l 119–122**: "if he could summon … Orpheus," (a pronoun the Latin lacks, with the name in apposition) now "if Orpheus could summon the shades of his wife,".
16. **l 124–125**: "the altars was holding" (ungrammatical); now "the altars he was holding".
17. **Note 133–136**: "`bis` commonly taken as once alive, and again after death" was an unsupported assertion; softened, and the infinitives (`innare`, `videre`, `indulgere`) now said to depend on `amor`/`cupido`.
18. **Note 146–147**: "simple present condition" with a future main verb, plus a garbled closing clause; rewritten (present indicative protasis, future apodosis; `fata` = fates).
19. **Note 140–141**: `decerpserit` "takes a future perfect or perfect subjunctive" (not a label); now: perfect subjunctive of anticipation, readable as future perfect; `quis` = anyone.
20. **i 106–109**: "sight and presence" dropped `ora` (face), so `l` and `i` disagreed; now "go before my dear father's eyes and look upon his face".

### Low
21. i 98–100: "wrapping truth in darkness" (echo of well-known versions) → "veiling the truth in dark sayings".
22. i 136–138 (golden bough): "golden in its leaves and in its pliant stem" echoes the usual wording → "a bough of gold — gold in its leaves and in its supple shoot — … sacred to the Juno of the underworld".
23. i 187–189 (golden bough wish): "If only that golden bough would show itself to us now, on its tree in so great a forest!" echoes known versions → "If that golden bough would only reveal itself to us now from its tree, in so vast a wood — since …".
24. i 162–165 (Misenus): "better at rousing men with the bronze and kindling war" echoes → "whom none surpassed in calling men up with the bronze, or in setting war alight with a tune".
25. i 125: "Born of the blood of gods" → "Scion of the blood of gods".
26. i 100–101: "the goad" for plural `stimulos` → "goads".
27. Note 128–129: "the English is built from the Latin and kept away from earlier versions" is process talk in a reader-facing note; replaced by "One of the best-known lines in the poem."
28. Note 158–159: "a dative with 'it comes'" ambiguous (it = eo); clarified.
29. Note 153: `pecudes` as "black cattle"; now "livestock, here the victims".
30. Note 185–186: "ipse stressing that he is not speaking yet" → "he himself, alone with his thoughts".
31. Note 187–189: `nemore in tanto` "preposition between adjective and noun" → noun and adjective.
32. Note 123: Aeneas's descent from Jupiter explained only by Venus; added Dardanus.
33. Note 142–143: added that `hoc … ferri` is accusative and infinitive after `instituit`.
34. ABOUT: "answers Aeneas's prayer in riddles" (she has just chanted her riddles, before he speaks) → "chants her riddling answer".

## Scan-fixes lines added (7)
6.103, 6.118, 6.147, 6.156, 6.169, 6.176, 6.183 (appended at the end of `scan-fixes.json`, each with its reason). Each entry matches the line's words under `WORD_RE` and has six feet, 13–15 syllables, one × (checked by a replica of the validator rule; the build was not run).

## Hand-scan results for the flagged and special lines
- **6.119** (packet flag, COSTLY 3.0): scanner is right, no entry. si po-tu | it Ma | nes ar | ces-se-re | con-iu-gis | Or-pheus; `-it` lengthened in arsis at the trithemimeral caesura, Mānes long-long, coniugis with consonantal i (con long by position), Orpheus two syllables (diphthong eu).
- **6.120** (Threïcia, eu-free): scanner's reading kept; it is forced by the metre (Threï- one syllable by synizesis, cīthara with long ī, fi-di both heavy). Doubt noted at R4.
- Greek eu / `heu` (150, 189): one long syllable, correct. Initial Ae- elsewhere (164 Aeoliden, 173 aemulus, 129 aequus, 165 aere, 171 aequora, 130 aethera): scanner correct (Ae- one syllable). Consonantal i (ianua 106, 127; iuvat 135; iussa 176; coniugis 119; Iove 123; Iuppiter 130; Iunoni 138): correct. Hiatus/elision at `hic` after elided `quando` (106) and `Misenum Aeoliden` (164): correct.
- All other lines: hand quantities agree with the scanner's marks.

## Refused findings
- **R1 (low) — speech mark at the head of `Dixit, pressoque obmutuit ore.`** The print has `aspicies. ”Dixit`; 5b asks that the reader see the corrected text, but `t` is cut from the pinned source and I may not touch it, so the closing ” still shows at the head of the Dixit unit in `t` (l and i close the speech correctly after `aspicies.`; the note records the misprint). Owner/caller could re-pin the source instead if wanted.
- **R2 (low) — 6.119 scan-fixes entry.** Considered because it was flagged; refused as the scanner's scansion is the correct one.
- **R3 (low) — l 102 "mouth" for plural `ora`.** The note already says it is a poetic plural; left.
- **R4 (low) — 6.120 quantities (fidibus, cithara).** Not changed; the metre forces the scanner's reading and I cannot confirm the natural lengths from L&S alone.
- **R5 (low) — set-piece i renderings kept**: "to go down to Avernus costs no effort", "the door of gloomy Dis is never shut, by night or by day", "there is the real work of it, there the hardship". Checked against memory of the well-known versions; none reproduces a distinctive wording (no "easy is the descent", no "night and day … open", no "this the task, this the toil").
- **R6 (low) — l 106–109 "my dear father".** `l` adds "my" the Latin lacks; acceptable as English filling, left.
- **R7 (low) — i 156–158 uses the past tense for the Latin historic presents.** Matches the register of the rest of the part; left.
